study type: Descriptive observational study and disproportionality analysis of individual case study reports
exposure: Use of selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs)
Use of serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor (SNRI) venlafaxine
Plasma drug concentrations of SSRIs/SNRIs (in-range vs. below-range)
outcome: Blood loss (>500 mL defined as PPH)
cohort: The study included individual case safety reports of PPH associated with SSRIs or venlafaxine from the FAERS database, and 43 pregnant women treated with an SSRI or SNRI for depressive or anxiety disorder who consented to plasma drug concentration monitoring at delivery.
finding: The mean blood loss in the below-therapeutic-range plasma concentration group was significantly higher than in the in-therapeutic-range group, suggesting that lower plasma levels of SSRIs/SNRIs do not reduce postpartum bleeding.
cross-section timing: At the time of delivery (for observational study), 14 years (for database analysis)
